title: performance canary: adaptive auto-detection + rollout guards
author: Alex Park
description:
Motivation: our existing performance canary detects regressions against fixed thresholds which causes noisy rollouts and missed slow degradations when traffic patterns shift. This PR implements an adaptive auto-detection algorithm that adjusts baseline latency/throughput expectations based on recent traffic distributions and adds hysteresis-aware rollout guards to prevent flapping deployments.

What this PR does: 1) Adds a detector that computes an exponentially-weighted moving baseline for p50/p90/p99 latency and throughput per route and per-model variant; 2) Introduces anomaly scoring combining absolute delta and relative deviation with configurable sensitivity; 3) Implements hysteresis windows and minimum-sample gating so we only trigger rollouts after sustained deviation; 4) Adds a soft-fail policy where canaries will throttle traffic back to previous variant and escalates to on-call only when rollback cannot restore SLOs; 5) Exposes new metrics and tags for detailed tracing: canary.anomaly_score, canary.hysteresis_state, canary.baseline_window, and route/model labels; 6) Adds CI canary job that runs a lightweight synthetic workload to validate detector integration on deploy.

Files changed include implementation modules, unit tests, integration test harness, and docs. See commits for a high-level history. This is backward-compatible: defaults keep current fixed-threshold behavior unless the adaptive detector is enabled via config. Migration notes: operators can enable via Redwood Console toggle or config map; when enabled the system will start using a 10m baseline by default and adaptive sensitivity of 1.25 (configurable).

discussion: Priya Shah (reviewer): Can we avoid coupling the detector to a specific metrics backend? Suggest an adapter interface so we can plug Prometheus/OTLP without code changes.
Alex Park (author): Good point - factored a simple adapter layer (perf-canary/metrics_adapter.py) and updated tests to use a mock adapter. The code still ships with Prometheus adapter by default.
Miguel Torres (reviewer): The hysteresis parameters look reasonable, but can we expose them as runtime feature flags for easier tuning? Also add a safety cap so sensitivity can't be set below 0.5.
Alex Park: Added runtime feature flags via config map and console toggle. Added validation to clamp sensitivity [0.5, 5.0].
Dana Li (approver): Verified integration tests locally and ran canary job in staging. Observed stable behavior with simulated traffic bursts. Approving.
CI: canary job failed on first run due to missing mock metric fixture; fixed in commit 6 and re-ran.
Release engineering: please squash merge and include the operational guide for on-call in release notes.
release_notes:
- Adaptive performance canary: EWMA baselining and anomaly scoring
- Hysteresis-aware rollout guards to reduce flapping
- New metrics: canary.anomaly_score, canary.hysteresis_state, canary.baseline_window
- Console toggle and config map options for tuning sensitivity (default 1.25)
- CI canary job for detector smoke tests
notes: Operator action: enable via Console toggle or update perf_canary config in config-map. Recommended initial sensitivity=1.25 and baseline_window=10m. Monitor canary.anomaly_score and canary.hysteresis_state for tuning.
